page: Amazon Web Services m5n.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an L3 cache of 35 MB, support for AVX-512 vector extensions, and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, does not include local storage, and contains no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes show that the m5n.8xlarge delivers mid-tier multi-threaded throughput while exhibiting lower single-core execution speeds. In stress-ng, it achieved a multi-core score of 27,089.93 against a single-core score of 1,285.59. Geekbench tests follow this trend, with a multi-core score of 9,940.0 compared to a single-core rating of 1,121.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (21.84 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (8.35 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile, whereas parallel workloads like software compilation (20,872.0) and ray tracing (20,037.0) align with mid-range industry averages. PassMark testing further reflects steady multi-core execution with a CPU score of 26,438.58 and a memory score of 2,622.65.

Data throughput and in-memory evaluation indicate reliable multi-core operations despite memory bandwidth tradeoffs under heavy uncached writes. Small cached blocks reach 1,507.36 GB/sec read speeds, but large uncached transfers taper to 105.41 GB/sec for reads and 46.68 GB/sec for writes. The instance sustained 25.86 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and reached 20.64 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference operates capably on smaller model scales, processing 1,008.63 prompt tokens per second on a 135M model and 39.64 tokens per second on a 7B model, but drops to 3.87 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5n.8xlarge is built for distributed applications that leverage high network bandwidth and parallel processing across its 32 vCPUs without needing expensive accelerated computing hardware. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached EBS storage, making the instance well matched for network-intensive multi-tier applications, caching layers, mid-scale enterprise databases, and parallel CI/CD build environments.
